summary.headline: IGI Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue and EBITDA each grew 21% YoY to INR 3,686 mn and INR 2,360 mn, with volumes up 16% to 3.64 mn reports.
summary.overview: Q4 (Jan–Mar 2026) was the first quarter reported after the switch from calendar to financial year, so the 15-month period (Jan 2025–Mar 2026) is the main comparison basis. Growth was led by lab-grown diamonds (LGD +35%) and LGD jewelry (+29%), while natural diamond jewelry fell 19% on gold and silver price volatility. The AGL acquisition (closed 30 Jan 2026) contributed about 2 pts to revenue and 3 pts to EBITDA growth in the quarter. Management guided to 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA growth for FY27 and said margins would be held at last year's levels.

financial_highlights.change: Mix shift to LGD and ND loose stones

financial_highlights.value: INR 2,963 mn from operations; total revenue INR 3,124 mn

financial_highlights.change: +21% YoY; margin down on US/Dubai commissions and INR 25 mn one-time AGL deal cost

segments.name: Lab-grown diamonds (LGD) loose
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +35% YoY (India standalone +46%); 15-month growth +25%. Management attributed the jump to new customer acquisitions and capacity additions at primary growers.

segments.name: Natural diamond jewelry
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue -19% YoY, attributed to India ND jewelry slowdown from steep gold and silver price rises; 15-month growth about +2%.

segments.name: Gemstones (AGL, acquired 30 Jan 2026)
segments.commentary: Reported within gemstone revenue; the quarter included about two months of AGL revenue, adding about 2 pts to group revenue growth and 3 pts to EBITDA growth. AGL financials are not disclosed separately.

segments.name: Subsidiaries (US, Dubai, Belgium, Netherlands)
segments.commentary: Subsidiary revenue grew about 14% and EBITDA over 25% in Q4, with margin up about 100 bps.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: about 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA growth, the same framework held for the past two years; management said FY27 volume growth could be 15–17%, with 20% volume growth and 15–16% revenue growth mentioned as broad guidelines.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at last year's levels; management said it will not allow margin erosion but is investing in AI/ML, brand building and US sales leadership.
Growth expected mainly from LGD capacity build-up and deeper penetration in natural diamonds, with AGL gemstone certification as a fifth segment.
Management said FY26 was ahead of the original guidance and that FY25 was over-delivered; the FY27 numbers are broad guidelines rather than firm targets.
Q4 is seasonally strong for LGD mix; management expects the LGD mix to taper through the year after Christmas and Diwali quarters.
capex_capacity: Lab-grown manufacturing capacity additions are happening mainly in Surat, India; management said the full impact of capacity additions has not yet shown in results and will ramp through FY27.
Industry expects LGD capacity to roughly double over the next three years, per management.
Management is building a US sales organisation with a new leadership recruit (3–4 months in role) and expanding the sales team there.
Plan to expand AGL color-stone certification beyond the US to other markets.
Employee benefit expense rose 16% QoQ (INR 71 cr in Q3 CY25, INR 73 cr in Q4 CY25, about INR 74 cr in Q1 CY26) as gemologist hiring continues in India and other geographies.
demand_pricing: Management said there were no structural changes to segment pricing in the quarter; mix shift toward higher-ASP LGD and ND loose stones drove the 4% ASP improvement.
Natural diamond jewelry in India weakened on gold and silver price volatility; management hopes conditions settle over the next one to two quarters.
Management estimates IGI holds about 20–25% of global natural diamond certification and over 50% in India, and is second globally behind the US market (these are internal estimates).
Management said 30–35% of natural and loose diamonds are uncertified, mainly small sizes with low commercial value, and that smaller studded stones are generally not certified at loose-stone level.
Retail demand for natural diamonds in bridal and high-value purchases was described as intact despite gold price volatility and macro uncertainty in some markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA growth achievable, and will INR depreciation help margins?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company has aimed for these growth rates for two years and expects them to continue. Margins are to be held at last year's levels despite investment in AI/ML, brand and the US sales organisation.

qa_highlights.question: Has LGD and ND pricing remained stable, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: No structural pricing changes in Q4. Mix is an outcome rather than a driver, and the company focuses on the growth of each segment.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the decline in natural diamond jewelry, and what is the US leadership progress?
qa_highlights.answer: The decline is attributed to gold and silver price increases and volatility in India. A new US leader has been in place for 3–4 months and the sales team is being strengthened.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs not rise after the gemologist hiring plan, and how do exports square with the growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost rose 16% QoQ as costs built up. Management said export values in rupees or dollars understate volume, since LGD carats have roughly doubled while value per carat has fallen.

qa_highlights.question: What is IGI's market share in natural diamonds, and why are 30–35% of stones uncertified?
qa_highlights.answer: IGI is second globally, with roughly 20–25% global share and over 50% in India (estimates). Uncertified stones are mostly small sizes with low commercial value.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers behind FY27 EBITDA growth exceeding revenue growth, and where is LGD capacity being added?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage, since incremental revenue flows largely to the bottom line. All LGD capacity additions are in Surat, India, while the US and Europe act as retail and marketing offices.

risks_watch: Natural diamond jewelry in India is under pressure from gold and silver prices; the company hopes for recovery within one to two quarters.
FY27 growth depends on LGD capacity ramp-up translating into volumes; the company says the full capacity impact has not yet shown.
Margin pressure from rising commission payouts to US and Dubai subsidiaries and from a 16% QoQ rise in employee costs, alongside AI/ML and brand spending.
Integration of AGL (acquired 30 Jan 2026) and its financial disclosure, which is not reported separately.
The company is not reporting an ASP outlook; management is focusing on volume, revenue and EBITDA instead, so mix and ASP will remain a source of questions.
Export data in value terms shows declines; the company says volume data is the right lens but does not disclose its own LGD carat figures.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the headline numbers and the long-term certification thesis, but defensive on the natural diamond jewelry slowdown and on export data. Several answers deflected specifics (market share, US team size, ASP), and the CFO repeatedly said the guidance is a broad framework rather than firm targets.
key_quotes: For Jan to March 2026 quarter, lab-grown diamond certification revenue grew by 35% year-on-year, while lab-grown jewelry certification grew by 29%.
We don't expect any erosion of the margins, so we will ensure our guidance for the year should be to maintain margins at the same levels as what we have seen in the last year.
We are committed to keep our certification on lab-grown as well as on natural diamond according to the 4Cs that has been there for nearly a century.
So long as we are able to deliver a 20% volume growth with a 15% to 16% revenue growth with a corresponding EBITDA growth, I think that should be what we should be focusing on.
